mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: A severe hail/wind threat will expand east-southeastward across northern Indiana into western Ohio this evening

details.label: Summary
details.text: A severe hail/wind threat will expand east-southeastward across northern Indiana into western Ohio this evening

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Thunderstorms have increased in coverage this evening across northern IN, likely aided by a weak mid-level disturbance noted on water vapor satellite imagery upstream across IL. Initial cells have undergone mergers, with multiple clusters ongoing. Ample low-level moisture and related very strong buoyancy will continue to support vigorous updrafts, even though stronger mid-level flow and related deep-layer shear will tend to remain a bit displaced to the north of the surface warm sector. Even so, enough shear should be present to support a mix of supercells and multicells in the short term (reference recent VWPs from KIWX). Severe hail generally up to 1-1.5 inches in diameter will be possible with any cells that can remain at least semi-discrete, while damaging winds may occur with any small clusters moving east-southeastward. An increase in the severe wind potential may develop across parts of northeast IN into northwest OH if a more dominant cluster can become established, as some short-term guidance suggests

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The potential for severe wind gusts is gradually waning across portions of the central High Plains. However, some potential will persist for the next 1-2 hours before the onset of nocturnal cooling

details.label: Summary
details.text: The potential for severe wind gusts is gradually waning across portions of the central High Plains. However, some potential will persist for the next 1-2 hours before the onset of nocturnal cooling

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Convection has begun to wane across northeast CO and much of the NE Panhandle with the exception of a cluster of storms over Cherry county, NE. This trend is largely due to the prevalence of expanding cold pools across the region with some locations observing temperature falls on the order of 10-15 F within the cold pools. Although some re-development is possible along the edges of the cold pools and/or along colliding outflow boundaries, the spatial extent of the deeply-mixed warm sector is quickly becoming limited. Some severe downburst potential should persist for the next 1-2 hours where outflow propagation and/or convective overturning has not yet occurred, but the onset of nocturnal cooling beyond 02 UTC will act to increase inhibition and further reduce the potential for deep convection. Northeastern portions of WW 559 will likely see a more prolonged severe wind, and perhaps hail, threat heading into the late evening hours where deep convection continues to mature on the western periphery of a more moist and strongly sheared air mass

details.label: Summary
details.text: An isolated hail/damaging wind threat may persist for another hour or so, but watch issuance is not expected at this time

details.label: Discussion
details.text: On the southern periphery of large-scale upper troughing over Ontario/Quebec, isolated thunderstorms have recently strengthened/moved into northern NY/VT. Favorable deep-layer shear (up to 40-45 kt) noted on the latest VWP from KCXX should continue to support updraft organization in the short term, with a small cluster moving across northern VT capable of producing damaging winds. Farther west, a cell moving into far northern NY may also pose an isolated threat for hail and gusty winds. However, the airmass across these areas is not overly unstable, and the loss of daytime heating should result in gradual stabilization of the boundary layer and an eventual weakening to ongoing thunderstorms. Therefore, watch issuance appears unlikely

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Satellite trends are being monitored for thunderstorm development across southeast Montana. If thunderstorms can develop they will likely move into an air mass very favorable for severe convection. Watch issuance is possible if this can occur

details.label: Summary
details.text: Satellite trends are being monitored for thunderstorm development across southeast Montana. If thunderstorms can develop they will likely move into an air mass very favorable for severe convection. Watch issuance is possible if this can occur

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest GOES imagery depicts a growing cumulus field across southeast Montana in proximity to a weak surface low/confluence zone. Although broad-scale forcing for ascent across this region is weaker compared to areas further south, the nearby thermodynamic environment appears supportive of thunderstorms with limited capping and around 2500 J/kg MLCAPE. It remains uncertain whether or not ascent across this region will be sufficient to initiate and maintain deep convection, and recent guidance shows considerable uncertainty on whether or not storms will develop (though a few RRFS solutions do hint at this potential). However, if convection can develop and be sustained, it will likely migrate east/southeast into an increasingly moist air mass where MLCAPE values increase to around 3000-4000 J/kg. Additionally, the KBIS VWP continues to sample 50-55 knot 0-6 km BWD, which will favor organized convection. Storm mode would likely transition from semi-discrete cells into an organized cluster/MCS given the relatively dry low-level air mass and weak near-surface flow within the zone of initiation, both of which would favor deep/expanding cold pools. If initiation and clustering occurs, a threat for large hail and severe winds will likely emerge across far southern ND and into northwest/north-central SD. Convective trends will continue to be monitored, and watch issuance will be considered if robust/sustained convection becomes more imminent

details.label: Watch probability
details.text: 40 percent
